question: On 3 January 2026, the United States carried out military strikes in Venezuela and abducted President Nicolás Maduro, who was subsequently taken to the United States to face charges. Following Maduro’s abduction, Venezuela’s Supreme Court appointed Vice-President Delcy Rodríguez as acting president, and diplomatic relations between Venezuela and the United States began to shift.

The Trump administration eased US sanctions on Venezuela’s oil industry and issued licences allowing US companies to buy, transport, store and refine Venezuelan crude. The United States completed its first sales of Venezuelan oil in January 2026 as part of a bilateral deal, and the administration stated that revenues from these oil sales would be managed and monitored by US authorities.

Can the Commission clarify the following: Is the Commission aware of Venezuelan oil, refined in the United States, being exported to or placed on the EU market, and of the quantities involved since January 2026?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) The importation of oil products into the EU must comply with any restrictive measures in force. The EU has in place restrictive measures concerning the situation in Venezuela (Council Regulation (EU) 2017/2063 of 13 November 20171) on 217 product categories.

However, those measures do not include restrictions on the importation of Venezuelan oil to the EU, either directly or indirectly. Exports of petroleum products from the US to the EU in the period from January to April 2026 were 1,8, 1,0, 0,9 and 1,5 million tons per month, respectively.
The Commission has data on the breakdown of the oil products imported but does not have data on the origin of the crude oil from which those petroleum products are produced in US refineries.
